note: mailbox_retired (v4, parent-free): {grant_id, provider, legacy}. Every v4 txn row projects source_mailbox (provenance.grant_id) and source_provider. The op retires the live rows that one mailbox imported before its position: rows whose source_provider equals provider and whose source_mailbox equals grant_id, or, when legacy is true, equals the account part of grant_id (before "/mbx-"). A retired row keeps every field, gets retired_by, and leaves liveByIngestID, byFingerprint and pendingByCurrency, so the same message imported again is a new row. Keep authors no op. Written by the Swift executor; the ledgerd TypeScript fold (schema 3, removed) and Go (no fold) do not model v4.
format: Each case is a conformance/replay case (log items of ops, expect.state blanked as there, expect.state_sha256 the pass condition), folded by the v4 fold.

cases.name: project
cases.note: Rows from two mailboxes and a manual row; each v4 import carries its mailbox and provider.

cases.name: retire-remove
cases.note: Remove retires mailbox A's two rows, the edited and annotated ones too; mailbox B and the manual row stay live.

cases.name: keep
cases.note: Keep authors nothing: the same log with no retire, every row live and counted.

cases.name: reconnect-after-remove
cases.note: After the retire the same mailbox is connected again: message 1 imports again under its ingest id as a new live row with no duplicate_ingest, and a new message imports as usual; the retired rows stay retired.

cases.name: old-rows-legacy
cases.note: Rows imported before grant ids named a mailbox carry the bare account id. With legacy true the Gmail retire takes the Gmail legacy row; the Outlook legacy row and another account's row stay.

cases.name: old-rows-left-alone
cases.note: The same log with legacy false: only the row that names mailbox A is retired.

cases.name: retire-malformed
cases.note: A retire with no legacy flag, or a provider outside [a-z0-9_]{2,32}, is an invalid_payload and retires nothing.
